rationale: Matthew also names Jesus "the son of Abraham" (40.1.1), and the genealogy traces the line back to Abraham by name (40.1.1-2, 17), which sets up a reading of this title against the promise of Genesis 12:1-3 that "all the families of the earth will be blessed through" Abraham's line. The label is "plausible" rather than "strong" because Davies and Allison, as reported by the Wikipedia article on Matthew 1:1 used here, caution that unlike "son of David," "son of Abraham" was not itself a recognized messianic title in this period but an expression that could describe any Jew; the tie to Genesis 12 specifically is this connection's own reading of the title against the genealogy's stated endpoint, not a documented title-to-promise usage.
